description: Shared cross-SDK E2E scenario manifest. ONE definition, executed by a thin interpreter in each SDK, so the three suites cannot drift. Declarative only: given a request, expect an outcome. Sponsored Pin tracking scenarios add `pinTracking`: the point-tracking calls an app makes on the served pins, as data, and the beacons that must reach the engine. Procedural scenarios (log capture, concurrency, retry, TTL waits) stay hand-written per SDK. Mirrored byte-identically into all three repos; a checksum test fails the build if the copies diverge. Every expected value here was verified against a live local decision-engine before being written. `fixtureScenarios` (schemaVersion 2) run offline: each decodes one golden decision-wire file (ui/platform/lib/ad-formats/golden-wire in adhub, shipped in this package under fixtures/golden-wire/) after optional `edits`, and asserts what the publisher's app reads from the decoded creative. `contentKeys` is the exact set of plain content keys (slides and matched points are asserted through their own fields); a key in `contentKeysAbsent` must decode as absent (null), never as an empty string or a placeholder; a null in `metadata` means absent. A runner that does not execute fixtureScenarios must refuse schemaVersion 2. A fixture scenario may add `slideTracking` (package 1.3.0, schemaVersion 3; a runner that does not execute it must refuse schemaVersion 3): `steps` the app takes on the decoded creative (`slideView`/`slideClick` with a 1-based slide index, `newResponse`, `fireClick` with a key or null for no key, `custom` with a key) and the beacons that must be dispatched: `beacons` is the exact ordered list of first-party beacons, each named by the tracker it must be (`slide`+`view`/`click`, or creative `click`/`custom`, with `response`), and `thirdPartyBeacons` the exact multiset of third-party tracker ids dispatched (their order is not asserted). An edit `at` `tracking` targets the creative's tracking object.

scenarios.title: a normal native ad serves with complete, well-formed metadata
a placement with no eligible ad returns a clean no-ad, not an error
the advertiser block is complete (name, legalName, logoUrl)
the template block carries a non-empty key
a served native ad exposes an impression URL, a click URL and non-empty contents
an ad whose creative is filled only in its default language serves in that language instead of an empty slot
count=2 returns at most two creatives, and they are distinct
three placements in one request each get their own correctly-keyed decision
an advertiserId filter still serves that advertiser's ad
format=native on a mixed placement returns a native ad
format=video on the same mixed placement returns a video ad instead
omitting format still serves — the engine chooses
a journey-owned placement and a normal placement resolve independently in ONE request
a non-skippable JSON video exposes json delivery and five video events (no skip)
a vast_tag ad exposes its tag URL and surfaces NO engine-side beacons (no double count)
a vast_xml ad exposes base64 that decodes to a VAST document, and no beacons
a skippable video resolves skippability from ENGINE METADATA, plus a sixth skip event
an end-card video reports its configured endCardMode
an unknown placement key raises a typed validation error, not a silent no-fill
an unknown custom-targeting key is rejected by the engine
the SDK deduplicates a repeated custom key, so the engine never sees the duplicate that would fail the whole request
scenarios.comment: Sent raw over HTTP this same payload returns 422 code 10031, and the engine aborts validation for the ENTIRE request — every placement, not just the offending target. All three SDKs dedupe by key (last write wins), so a publisher cannot reach that state through the public API. This scenario is the live proof of that guard: it must SERVE, and both placements must come back.

scenarios.title: a single valid custom target does not break serving
a count above the documented maximum is rejected
a request with no placements fails locally, before any network call
API version 2025-01-01 still serves a native ad and never a journey block
omitting the version header still serves (engine falls back to the oldest active version)
a radius search returns the campaign's own shops, nearest first
a bounds search returns them too — the other shape a map can ask with
every returned shop carries its own view, tap and click beacons
every returned shop carries a resolved destination, its own or the creative's
the request's limit narrows how many shops come back
a tight radius excludes the shops outside it
without a distance search a Sponsored Pin campaign does not serve at all
on the older API version the ad still serves, silently carrying no pins — the failure an integrator must recognise
a map's first render sends every shop's view beacon exactly once
re-rendering the same response sends no view beacon again
a render that brings new shops into view sends views only for the new ones
a new decision response reports the same shops again, once
single-pin views follow the same once-per-response rule as the bulk call
taps and clicks are sent on every call, never de-duplicated
a Card with only its required content serves under the Card standard
a Card with every optional content serves them all, in a style the standard defines
an Expandable Banner with only its required content serves under the Expandable Banner standard
an Expandable Banner with every optional content serves them all
a Branded Asset with only its required content serves with its asset context
a Branded Asset with every optional content serves them all, with its asset context
a Standard Video with only its required content serves under the Standard Video standard
a Standard Video with every optional content serves them all
a standard Ad whose creative cannot satisfy its standard's contract is not served
a legacy creative names no standard and carries no asset context
a Journey screen that cannot satisfy its standard is skipped and the next stage's screen answers
a Journey screen serves the Card style saved on it
a Carousel with only its required content serves its slides in order, each with the slide tracking the app needs
a Carousel with every field serves three slides, each carrying all five slide contents
a Carousel whose second slide misses its required image is not served, because a slide is never dropped to make a Carousel valid
a slide clicked before its view was sent sends the view, then the click, and the engine accepts both
a slide clicked after its view sends only the click, on every click, and the engine accepts them
a slide shown twice sends its view beacon once per response
a Carousel has no creative-level click: fireClick sends nothing
a Journey screen on the Carousel standard serves its slides in order, each with its own slide tracking, and no screen click
on a Journey slide, a view then taps send slide_view once per slide and one default click per tap, and the engine accepts every beacon
a template based on Native Display that adds a video serves the video as one of its contents

fixtureScenarios.title: a Native Display creative exposes its standard format, version and template source
a Native Display creative leaves every optional field it was served without absent
a template based on a standard keeps the standard's identity and exposes the operator's addition by key
a Carousel exposes its slides in server order, each with its id, position, contents and own trackers, and no creative-level click
a minimal Carousel still exposes its slides and leaves the optional brand logo and disclaimer absent
a Carousel based on a standard exposes its slides and the operator's addition
a Tap-to-expand creative exposes expand and close as custom events, apart from its click
a minimal Tap-to-expand creative leaves its optional texts absent and keeps expand and close
a Branded Assets creative exposes asset tap as a custom event, apart from its click
a Branded Assets creative without a destination has no click, only the asset tap
a Standard Video exposes its video events and click, and no skippable setting
a Standard Video without a destination has no click action or click tracker
a Sponsored Pin creative keeps decoding its matched points as it does today
a Sponsored Pin creative with only its pin image and no destination has no creative-level click tracker
fixtureScenarios.comment: Only pinImage is required. With no destination on the creative or on the pin, the creative and the pin carry no click tracker (an empty list, never a click that opens nothing) and the point has no clickUrl; its view and tap stay. This scenario checks only the creative-level click (clickKeys); the per-pin tracking.clicks and the absent clickUrl are checked by decode only, and the engine side is pinned by sponsored_pin_serving.feature.

fixtureScenarios.title: a creative served before the standards (gate off) decodes as today, with the three standard fields absent
fixtureScenarios.comment: The engine omits the three standard fields while is_standard_native_formats_enabled is off; this is that wire. Absent means null, never an empty string or a placeholder (BR-SDK-01, BR-SDK-09).

fixtureScenarios.title: fields the SDK does not know yet, at any level, never break decoding
fixtureScenarios.comment: An additive field the engine starts sending later must be ignored, not fail the response (BR-SDK-01).

fixtureScenarios.title: a slide's view beacon is sent once per served response, however often the slide is shown
fixtureScenarios.comment: Keyed on the signed view URL, never on the slideId: re-rendering or scrolling back to a slide must not count it again (BR-SDK-04, Q19).

fixtureScenarios.title: the same slide in a new decision response counts again
fixtureScenarios.comment: A new response carries new signed URLs for the same slides. The runner simulates it by decoding the same golden file again with every first-party tracker URL suffixed `&response=N` (N = 2, 3, ...); `response` in an expected beacon names which one (default 1).

fixtureScenarios.title: a slide clicked before its view was sent sends the view, then the click, then the creative's applicable third-party click trackers once
fixtureScenarios.comment: Applicable means a click tracker matching any click, or the `default` click specifically; a tracker for another click key and an impression tracker do not fire (BR-SDK-05, Q14, Q18).

fixtureScenarios.title: a slide clicked after its view sends only the click, on every click
slide views never send third-party click trackers
a Carousel has no creative-level click: fireClick sends nothing, so slide clicks go through the slide helper
fixtureScenarios.comment: Publishers must not route a slide tap through fireClick (BR-SDK-03, Q9).

fixtureScenarios.title: fireClick with no key sends the default click of a standard
fixtureScenarios.comment: Every standard seeds its click with key `default`, which is what fireClick sends without a key (BR-SDK-06, Q12).

fixtureScenarios.title: expand and close are sent verbatim as custom events and are not clicks
fixtureScenarios.comment: The publisher calls them when the banner actually expands or closes; no click is sent and no third-party click tracker fires (BR-SDK-07).

fixtureScenarios.title: an asset tap is sent verbatim as a custom event and is not a click
a Standard Video without a destination sends no click
fixtureScenarios.comment: No destination means no click action and no click tracker (BR-SDK-08).
